objective_for_doctor: A 26-year-old M patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: fever.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve had a fever, coughing, and I’ve been coughing up blood. I also have pain that feels burning and is sensitive, with intensity 7/10, and it’s located in my tonsil (left), the thyroid cartilage, palate, pharynx, and under the jaw.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—how long have you had the fever and the blood in your cough, and is the blood bright red or darker/clotted?  
Doctor: Also, do you smoke, have any recent sore throat/neck injury or dental infection, and have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes or trouble swallowing/breathing?
I don’t know.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—do you have any shortness of breath or worsening throat pain when swallowing, and have you had fevers/chills for more than 3 days?  
Doctor: Also, can you check your temperature if possible, and tell me whether the blood is bright red vs dark/coffee-ground and how much (streaks vs more)?
I don't know.

Doctor: I need a few quick specifics: can you look in the mirror and tell me if you have visible swelling or a new lump under the jaw/neck, and do you have trouble swallowing saliva (drooling) or a muffled “hot potato” voice?  
Doctor: Also, estimate the blood amount—just streaks when you cough, or more than that (roughly teaspoons/coughing up clots)?
I don’t know.

Doctor: I can’t make progress if you “don’t know”—please answer these as best you can: 1) is the cough blood **only streaks** or **more than streaks/clots**, and 2) do you have **trouble swallowing** or **drooling/muffled voice** right now?  
Doctor: Also, can you do a quick self-check: is the pain **one-sided only** (left) and do you have **neck/jaw swelling** or a **bad tooth/foul-smelling breath**?
It’s on the left—my pain is located in my tonsil (L). I don’t know about trouble swallowing, drooling, a muffled voice, neck/jaw swelling, or bad tooth/foul-smelling breath.

Doctor: Thanks—next, please tell me: do you have any shortness of breath, chest pain, or dizziness (even mild), and are you currently able to swallow liquids without choking?  
Doctor: Also, when did this start (number of days), and have you had any recent dental work, upper-respiratory infection, or known COVID/flu exposure?
I don't know.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—1) how many days ago did the fever/cough with blood start, and 2) do you have any shortness of breath or dizziness right now (yes/no)?  
Doctor: Also, do you have trouble swallowing liquids or is it normal?
I don't know.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—this is important: can you tell me your best guess on two yes/no items: (1) any **shortness of breath** right now, and (2) any **trouble swallowing liquids** (choking/coughing when drinking)?  
Doctor: Also, please answer: how many days has this been going on, and do you have any **history of bleeding** (nose/gums) or are you on **blood thinners/aspirin/NSAIDs**?
I don’t know.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—please answer as best you can: are you on any blood thinners/aspirin/ibuprofen, and have you had any nosebleeds or bleeding gums recently? Also, about how many days total has the fever + cough with blood been going on?  
Doctor: If you truly can’t answer, tell me what your temperature was at any point (even if approximate) and whether the blood is only in the cough or also in saliva otherwise.
I don’t know.

Doctor: I need at least some measurable details to decide safely—can you check your pulse/oxygen level if available (SpO2) and tell me your approximate age and current temperature, plus whether the blood is only when coughing or also in your saliva?  
REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential  
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray  
REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_profile_(PT_INR_PTT)
I don’t know.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—right now I’m concerned about hemoptysis (coughing blood) with fever, but you can’t provide key symptoms; I need you to get objective vitals if possible (current temperature, heart rate, SpO₂) and whether you can swallow normally.  
Doctor: Please also complete the ordered tests I requested—CBC with differential, chest X‑ray, and coagulation profile (PT/INR/PTT)—so I can decide on the safest likely diagnosis and next step.
I don’t know.

Doctor: I can’t safely diagnose hemoptysis with fever when you can’t tell me any key symptoms or provide any vitals—please measure now: temperature, heart rate, and SpO₂ if you can, and confirm whether you’re on any blood thinners/aspirin or have had any recent nose/gum bleeding.  
Doctor: Meanwhile I’m ordering/confirming results ASAP: REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential, REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray, REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_profile_(PT_INR_PTT).  
Doctor: If you have shortness of breath, are coughing up more than small streaks, or feel faint, go to the ER immediately.
I don’t know. I have been coughing up blood, I have a fever, and I have a cough. I’m also immunosuppressed.

Doctor: Thank you—since you’re immunosuppressed and still having fever with coughing up blood, I need vitals now: what are your current **temperature, heart rate, and SpO₂** (if available), and are you having **shortness of breath** right now?  
Doctor: Also, do you take any **blood thinners** (warfarin/apixaban/rivaroxaban), **aspirin**, or frequent **NSAIDs** (ibuprofen), and how much blood is it (just streaks vs teaspoons/clots)?
I don’t know. I have been coughing up blood, I have a fever, and I have a cough. I’m also immunosuppressed.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—since you’re immunosuppressed and having fever with coughing up blood but can’t provide vitals or bleeding details, this is potentially serious; do you currently have shortness of breath, chest pain, dizziness, or are you coughing up more than just streaks?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential; REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray; REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_profile_(PT_INR_PTT); REQUEST TEST: CMP; REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Gram_stain_and_culture (if you can expectorate).
I don’t know. I have been coughing up blood, I have a fever, and I have a cough. I’m also immunosuppressed.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—given immunosuppression plus fever and active hemoptysis, I’m treating this as potentially life-threatening until proven otherwise: please go to the ER now for immediate assessment with the tests we ordered (CBC w/diff, PT/INR/PTT, CMP, chest X-ray) and notify them you’re immunosuppressed and coughing blood.  
Doctor: If you can, also tell me one last thing: are you short of breath right now (yes/no)?
I don’t know. I have been coughing up blood, I have a fever, and I have a cough. I’m also immunosuppressed.

Doctor: Given you’re **immunosuppressed** with **fever + coughing up blood (hemoptysis)** and you can’t provide vitals or bleeding details, this is high-risk—please proceed to the **ER immediately** for assessment and the ordered tests (**CBC w/ diff, PT/INR/PTT, CMP, Chest X‑ray**).  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Potential serious infection causing hemoptysis (e.g., pneumonia with hemoptysis vs opportunistic lung infection such as tuberculosis/fungal disease); rule out life-threatening pulmonary causes—ER required.
